title: CareLoop simulator scenario
description: A SYNTHETIC test journey in two parts. The steps are hospital-system events that the HIS simulator replays against CareLoop's FHIR boundary. The behaviour on each patient says how that patient reacts when CareLoop notifies them, which the patient-channel simulator applies when a notification actually arrives. Clinical values (result category, urgency, closure reason) are placeholder codes that must exist in the pathway definition; a scenario never invents clinical content.

name.description: Scenario key; equals the file name without extension.

synthetic.description: Must be true. Marks every record produced by the scenario as simulated.

pathwayId.description: Identifier of the pathway definition the scenario runs against.

syntheticId.description: Synthetic patient identifier; always prefixed SYN-.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag used to pick message templates.

id.description: Stable step identifier; used to build a deterministic source event ID.

at.description: ISO 8601 duration offset from scenario start, for example PT0S or P2D.

actor.description: Which simulator performs the step. Only the HIS simulator performs steps: a patient's reactions are never scripted as steps, they follow from patients[].behaviour when a notification arrives.

action.description: The kind of event to emit. One value per event type a hospital system sends to CareLoop.

caseRef.description: Local handle for the case (one actionable result) the step belongs to.

patientRef.description: Required on screening-result; refers to patients[].ref.

status.description: Track or task status carried by the step, for example accepted, rejected, fulfilled, noshow.

params.description: Action-specific values. Clinical values must be placeholder codes from the pathway definition.

patientBehaviour.description: How the simulated patient reacts when CareLoop notifies them. The patient-channel simulator applies it each time a notification for this patient arrives. It is a reaction, not a timetable: if CareLoop never sends a notification, nothing is reported and nothing is acknowledged.

delivery.description: What the channel reports for a notification: deliver = delivered; fail = delivery failed, with failureReason; silent = the message is accepted but no delivery report is ever sent.

failureReason.description: Why delivery failed. Required when delivery is fail.

response.description: What the patient does after a delivered notification: none = stays silent; acknowledge = confirms they saw it; understand = confirms they understood (teach-back); call-me = asks for a call. Only possible when delivery is deliver.

respondAfter.description: ISO 8601 duration between delivery and the response, for example PT1H. Defaults to PT0S.

respondToNotification.description: Which notification the patient responds to, counting the notifications this patient has received. 1 (the default) is the first; 2 describes a patient who only reacts to a reminder. Earlier notifications get the delivery behaviour and no response.

role.description: Demo role key, for example clinician, coordinator, facility-lead.

seed.description: Random seed so a cohort replays identically.

scenario.description: Name of a step-based scenario in this folder.

expectation.description: What the journey and end-to-end tests assert after the scenario has run.
